text:
Pikachu has hosted a lot of parties over the years, but never one this big. A month from now, Pokémon steps onto a stage it’s never touched before, which is saying something, since the recent Pokémon Worlds celebration was massive in its own right.

With multiple musical guests, events, and organized play in both the card game and video game realms, a lot was going on in the Pokémon world just a few weeks ago, but the fun is mostly over now. Thankfully, that changes very soon. Thanks to an update from The Pokémon Company, the Pokémon Night Out event plans are finally laid out for everyone to see.

Trading its usual battle arenas for a sold-out dance floor at Intuit Dome in Los Angeles, Pokémon Night Out brings the franchise face-to-face with EDM for the first time. Headlining the night of October 24 is Marshmello, the producer whose masked stage presence has become as recognizable in dance music as Pikachu is in and beyond the Pokémon franchise.

Joining him is Australian DJ Alison Wonderland, rounding out a lineup built specifically for this crossover rather than a generic festival circuit. Both artists have talked openly about growing up with Pokémon before, so this isn’t just a licensing deal stitched together for headlines. More like two fandoms finally getting the show they've wanted for years, isn’t it?

The franchise has spent three decades on handhelds, trading card tables, and Saturday morning television, and now it’s testing whether that same energy translates to a live music set themed around Pokémon.

Attendees can expect stage technology and Pokémon-themed visual storytelling designed to bring the franchise to life in a way fans haven’t seen before, according to the press materials. The event is also age-restricted: tickets were limited to fans 16 and older.
